description.narrative: The Institutional Reform Development Policy Grant (IR DPG) will support the Government's Reform Strategy, as discussed in the country assistance strategy (CAS). It emphasizes two key elements: 1) Supporting non-oil growth through investment climate reforms through: a) Rationalizing the incentive framework (by harmonizing treatment of income, expenses and investment with international standards); b) Strengthening property rights (by reducing ambiguity of land titling and improving public management of land registration); and 2) Strengthening governance and public financial management through: a) Reforming procurement as part of public financial management reforms to increase transparency and accountability and to separate the policy-making functions from the administrative function; b) Supporting the public administration reform strategy, in particular through wage policy, retrenchments and a biometric database on public employees as part of broader civil service reform; and c) Increasing revenue transparency through Yemen's accession to the Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (EITI). The project will contribute to accelerate growth, poverty alleviation and improved governance through its provisions, which comprise key parts of the Government's overall growth strategy.

The project supports the implementation of key elements of the government's reform program. It focuses on two pillars of the broader country strategy: (i) increasing non-oil growth; and (ii) strengthening governance.

baseline.value: Adherence to the provisions of the wage law and of specific decrees relating to each phase of wage increase.

target.value: Fulfillment of provisions of wage law and of decrees relating to each phase of wage increase.

actual.value: Partly achieved. In July 2005 the minimum wage was increased from YR7,400 to YR20,000, equivalent to the poverty line. In October2007, the wage structure was revised to increase the compression ratio to 1:4. The wage increases were based on the implementationof a unified wage and grade structure (as specified in article 23 of the wage law). The one exception is Article 29, whichrefersto the need for the Ministry of Civil Service and Insurance to prepare an integrated standard system of employmentdescription and evaluation prior to implementation. Based on the information provided by the government, GoY has brought thesalary structure into conformity with a unified system of classifying civil servants to a unified system of classification with 6occupational levels and 20 grades. However, the job description study as part of the CSMP was completed late # in 2009 -- after thewage increases. The wagelaw also calls for the establishment of a consolidated employee database having branch units connected to acentral database which has not been achieved.

comment.narrative: Vague wording of original law complicates evaluation.

target.value: Civil Service Fund targes for redundancies met. Wage Law provisions adhered to, including achievmeent of second round targets. Biometric identification program complete (# employees, % covered).

title.narrative: Implementation of the civil service fund program for June 2007-May 2008.

target.value: Achievement of targets (including retrenchments) for specified period.

actual.value: Achieved. The Civil Service Fund (CSF) was created to facilitate the processing redundancies from the civil service, identifiedthrough the civil service reforms. To date, a total of 7 batches of redundant civil servants have been transferred to the CSFbetween 2006 and 2009. During this period a total of 14,127 redundant civil servants have been referred to the CSF divided asfollows: (1) 2,250 referred to statutory pension; (2) 1,100 redeployed to other civil service units; and (3) 10,777 processed bythe CSF compensation system. Between June 2007 and May 2008 a total of 5,350 civil servants were processed by the CSF. No specifictargets were established during this period against which to evaluate this achievement, but the objective of having an operationalinstitution processing redundant employees was met.

baseline.value: EITI acceded to but accounts not yet audited under EITI procedures and reviewed with relevant stakeholders.

actual.value: Achieved. The Yemen EITI Council was fully operational and issued a reconciliation report covering three years of extractiveindustries payments and corresponding public revenues in late October, 2010. The report, entitled Yemen First EITI ReconciliationReport2005, 2006 and 2007 was then distributed in early November at a major, well-attended workshop covered in the press andpublished onthe Yemen EITI website (www.yemeneiti.org). This report was reviewed and approved by an expert World Bank advisor andstaff.

title.narrative: Rationalized incentives facing private investors through treatment of income, investment and expenses.

baseline.value: High marginal rates, use of tax holidays and incentives created dramatically different marginal effective tax rates for firms in different sectors, of different sizes. METRs ranging from -20% to 61%.

target.value: Low marginal rate of CIT, homogeneous METRs across sectors and firm characteristics.

actual.value: Work with FIAS/PEP-MENA. Government drafted new law with lower rates, few exceptions, universal incentives; is integrating incentives under customs and investment laws into tax code.

title.narrative: Creation of a system of secure and enforceable property rights.

baseline.value: Imperfect legal titling requires title to be verified through judicial action; high rate of conflict over land title. Land registry not legally independent, GALSUP mandate unclear.

target.value: Legally conclusive land title available. Independent land registrar established. Clear mission established for GALSUP. Reduced legal conflict over land title.

actual.value: New land registration law submitted to parliament. Progress to be determined on supervision mission.

actual.value: Partly achieved. The condition was partly met by inclusion of 100% of core civil service employees and over 87% of security andmilitary employees.

title.narrative: Establishment of a procurement policy monitoring Board.

baseline.value: Procurement policy monitoring board was not yet established.

target.value: Procurement policy monitoring board in place and utilizing procurement information system for monitoring.

actual.value: Achieved. The board, named the #Higher Authority on Tender Control,# was legally established by Presidential Decree No. 17 of2009as a new policy and monitoring oversight Board nominated by the Shura Council and appointed by the President of the Republic.The HATC is staffed and operational. It has set up an interim procurement policy management information system (PMIS), taking intoaccount World Bank advice, through its website (www.hatcyemen.org).

title.narrative: Strenghening of PFM and governance with regard to public expenditure through procurement reform.

baseline.value: Procurement system not in full compliance with international best practice. Timely information on procurement not available or actively monitored. High Tender Board (HTB) not fully independent.

target.value: Executive regulations in place. HTB independence established as apex body of procurement operations in public procurement system. Procurement policy monitoring board, PIM in place, active.

actual.value: New procurement law enacted. Procedural reforms underway. Procurement Information System project being implemented.

title.narrative: Council of Ministers has issued a decree defining the mandate and functions of the General Authority for Lands, Survey and Urban Planning (GALSUP).

baseline.value: The mandate for GALSUP was not defined.

target.value: Ministerial Decree defining GALSUP mandate approved.

actual.value: The President of Yemen issued Presidential Decree no (82) of 2009 establishing the Organizational Decree for the General Authorityfor Land, Survey and Urban Planning (GALSUP). The decree specifies the mandate of GALSUP, including its objectives, functions andresponsibilities, management, governance structure, and organizational structure as well as the functions and responsibilities ofitssubordinate units. The decree was reviewed by a land policy expert employed by the World Bank in November of 2009 anddetermined tobe acceptable.
